utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point in time, Your Honour, I have this witness here. I tried to get this from the witness in view of his statement. And I'm sure that there will be other witnesses that will speak about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Lee, I think we should leave it to that at this moment. Mr. Stojanovic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more area briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Svraka, my understanding was that during one of these operations the doctors warned you that in the abdominal area you have a shrapnel that was still there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Could you please re-start your answer because the interpreters could not hear you. So the question was whether they warned you that in the abdominal area there was still shrapnel. Is that correct. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, just a moment, please. It was my leg that was operated on. One was cut off and the other one was stitched up. Mended. And when I woke up in this room that used to be called intensive care, and the first time they asked me, Grandpa, where you feel pain? I mean, I was a grandfather even then. And I said it's my stomach. Judges, Your Honours, it was my stomach that was painful, and they touched me and they said, Has to be operated on. Had I not said that I felt pain in my stomach I would have died, not because of the leg but because of the stomach. I was in a coma or sleeping or whatever it was during two days. I mean, I don't even know when I woke up. It's not that I kept a calendar or something, and had I not said that I had a stomachache I would have died on account of my stomach. But anyway, when I woke up, Dr. Milosevic had performed an operation on me. He was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear Mr. Stojanovic. He is not speaking into his microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the interpreters cannot hear you if you do not talk into the microphone. You're turning it even further away from you, but ... Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I'm sorry. I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now this is what I'd like to ask you. After this operation, did you keep the shrapnel that the doctors took out?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SVRAKA
utterances.text: I kept it for years at home. It was as big as a cube of sugar, and I have my letters of discharge of all the operations --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But my point was that you do not have it any longer.

utterances.speaker: ISMET SVRAKA
utterances.text: I don't have it in my stomach anymore. I don't have it at home anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm sorry if this was too much of a burden for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This concludes then your cross-examination. Ms. Lee, is there any need to ask further questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: I just wanted to make one -- have this witness make one clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I hope it's on a relevant matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Mr. Svraka, during cross-examination, you were asked: "Can you tell me whether you had an opportunity to see from which direction this shell could have come?" And your answer was: "In the direction of the street, because this market building, and if you have a tram tracks and you have buildings on both sides that are 10, 15, 20 metres high, I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm referring to transcript, page 63, and line 5 was the question and line 7 it begins -- is where Mr. Svraka has given his answer. My question to you is: In your examination-in-chief, you said that you did not hear or see any shell before -- I mean, you did not see where -- you did not hear the shell come from anywhere and you did not see the shell. In this question when you were asked when you had the opportunity to see from which direction this shell could have come, and you say direction [indiscernible] -- on that day, did you actually see the shell come before it landed 5 to 7 metres?

utterances.speaker: ISMET SVRAKA
utterances.text: I didn't see it. I just heard it. No one can see a shell in the air. I heard it explode and hit me. I mean, almost killed me. Maybe it would have been better had it killed me. I heard the explosion of a shell and where it came from and who threw it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you, Ms. Lee. Mr. Svraka --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- since the Chamber has no further questions for you, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague, and we're fully aware that travelling is certainly not easy for you in your present physical condition. Therefore, thank you very much, both for coming and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the usher assist Mr. Svraka in leaving the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you indicated that you wanted to raise a matter which would take you five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it occurs to me that there's another way that the Chamber might be able to make some productive use of this time. Today the Prosecution has tendered two videos of the Markale -- of the incident, P446 and P448. We did not show this witness the entire video in court in an effort to be sensitive to the witness with respect to what is graphic and difficult to watch video. Your Honour, with respect to P446, the Prosecution will be playing the entirety of that tape later this week with RM110, an investigator. However, with respect to P448, it is -- there is no witness at the present for which the Prosecution intends to play the entirety of that tape. It is four to six minutes long, and I wonder whether that -- if the Chamber wishes, we would be prepared to play that for the Chamber now so we could view that video. And I do still have my five-minute submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, any objections to P448 to be played now?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour. I mean, in order to get a clear idea in terms of what the witness had been speaking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Groome, the Chamber grants leave to play P448 in its entirety at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before I ask Ms. Stewart to do it, I would note that although the tape does contain some ambient sound, the Prosecution does not rely on anything that is said on the tape. And with that, I would ask Ms. Stewart to please play the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes the playing of P448. In addition to that, Your Honour, there are two other matters that first can be dealt with in open session, and the second I will ask that we go into private session. Your Honours, last Monday on 29 October the Prosecution omitted to tender one associated exhibit for the witness Grgo Stojic, a witness with no protective measures. At this stage I would like to tender that exhibit now. It is 65 ter 06374. It is a report from a health centre in Sanski Most dated the 9th of November, 1992. It contains a description of the nine bodies of the named victims in the indictment, their position, clothes they were wearing, and entry/exit wounds, and of course I understand if my colleagues on the Defence would seek to respond to this tomorrow morning, but I did want to correct that omission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any response yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would appreciate a chance to review the document, see which one it is. I believe this one might even have been tendered as a Defence exhibit, but I'm not certain at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will then hear from you on 65 ter 06374. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of my colleagues tells me that it was used by the Defence but not tendered by you. Well, if you used it, would there be any objection against having --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection, then. That's why I thought it was the document. So no objection to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Madam Registrar, 65 ter 06374, would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P449, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P449 is admitted into evidence. The second matter you'd like to raise in private session, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, the 6th of November, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III.
